verse.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.

verse.line: The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

prasang.title: Marks of the knower and the doer
prasang.summary: The disciplined person acts without attachment, like a lotus leaf untouched by water, and finds peace by letting go of the fruit.
prasang.lesson: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna about how to act in the world without being stained by it. He says that the person who gives up the payoff of their actions finds lasting peace, while the one who chases the result and is driven by desire remains bound. This means you can live inside the work, in the mess and the effort, without letting the result soak into you or decide your state. The result is just what comes next, not the ground beneath your feet.
verse.for_you: The first customer is real, but the result is not your footing. Let the work itself be the ground. Do not let the next outcome decide if you are at peace.

verse.speaker: Bhartrihari
verse.sanskrit: निन्दन्तु नीतिनिपुणा यदि वा स्तुवन्तु लक्ष्मीः समाविशतु गच्छतु वा यथेष्टम् । अद्यैव वा मरणमस्तु युगान्तरे वा न्याय्यात्पथः प्रविचलन्ति पदं न धीराः ॥
verse.line: Let them praise or blame, let money come or go: the steady don't step off the right path.
verse.translation: Let the worldly-wise blame or praise; let fortune come or go as she pleases; let death come today or ages hence: the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right.
verse.why: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

prasang.title: Nitishatakam: On steadfastness
prasang.summary: Steadfastness: the gods kept churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar; the steady do not leave the right path whatever people say. A struck ball bounces back and a cut tree grows again.
prasang.lesson: Setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path.

verse.meaning: Bhartrihari speaks to the reader from the section on steadfastness. He says that whether the worldly-wise praise or blame, whether fortune comes or goes, or whether death comes today or ages hence, the steadfast do not move a step from the path of what is right. The idea is that setbacks rarely last for those who keep going on the right path. The story around this shows the gods churning the ocean past jewels and poison until they found nectar.
verse.for_you: You have the first paying customer now, and that is real. The next twelve months will ask you to keep going on the right path even when the money comes and goes. Let that work itself be your footing, not the praise or the worry about what comes next.

verse.ref: Mahabharata · Vana Parva · Vana: Draupadi and Yudhishthira
verse.speaker: Draupadi
verse.setting: Draupadi argues that waiting on fate is no plan: people must act.
verse.sanskrit: कुर्वतो नार्थसिद्धिर्मे भवतीति ह भारत / निर्वेदो नात्र गन्तव्यो द्वावन्तौ यस्य कर्मणः
verse.line: Don't despair because effort hasn't paid off yet. Every attempt can go either way.
verse.translation: 'I keep working and still don't succeed' is no reason to despair. Every effort can end two ways, in success or not; only by not acting is the outcome certain.
verse.why: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

prasang.title: Do right without reward, and keep working
prasang.summary: Draupadi questions a world where the good suffer; Yudhishthira answers that he does right because it is right, not for reward. Draupadi replies that effort still matters: fate rewards no one who waits.
prasang.lesson: Do right for its own sake, then work as if it all depends on you.

verse.meaning: Draupadi is speaking to Yudhishthira in the forest. He has given up, certain that his good deeds have brought him nothing. She tells him that saying 'I did my part and still failed' is no reason to stop trying. Every attempt can go two ways, success or failure, and the only way to be sure of losing is to do nothing. Do what is right because it is right, then work as if the result depends entirely on your own hands.
verse.for_you: The customer you signed yesterday is real, but so is the doubt that follows. Do the work for the work's own sake, and trust that showing up today is its own reward.

script: You signed the customer yesterday after fourteen months of work. You know the hard part is here now. The mind wants to believe this first win is the whole thing, or that the next step is impossible. That is the moment you are in.

Arjuna stood on the battlefield and asked Krishna what happens to a person who tries to walk the path and then falls away. He feared that such a one was lost, like a torn cloud blown away by the wind. Krishna answered that no sincere effort is ever wasted. Krishna said:
प्रयत्नाद्यतमानस्तु योगी संशुद्धकिल्बिषः, अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्.
In plain words: The one who keeps at it, steadily, over a long time, gets there.

This is easier said than done, because the mind wants a single leap to finish everything. But the texts say the work itself is the ground beneath you. If you fall, you rise again. The effort you made yesterday is not erased. It carries forward into today, and you simply continue. That is how you stay grounded.
When the anxiety rises about the next month, do not look for a big sign. Look for the next small task that belongs to your work, and do it. That is the steadiness you are looking for.
The work itself becomes the ground beneath you.
